newsitem.title: DENMARK: Firm crown nudges Danish bond prices up.
newsitem.headline: Firm crown nudges Danish bond prices up.

text.p: Danish benchmark bond prices ended Monday below their opening level but up on Friday's close and dealers said that the firm crown currency was sending buyers toward the shorter paper.

"If the crown continues to advance it will lead to greater interest at the short end of the market," a trader said adding that he expected German indicators due this week to send Danish prices higher.
The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 closed at 105.80, up 0.20 from Fridaay's close but down 0.10 from its Monday opening, in turnover of 3.1 billion crowns.
Its September future, which expired at closing time to be replaced by the December contract, was untraded at 105.48.
The December future rose 0.82 to 104.74, with 586 contracts traded.
The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.45 point to 83.50.
The crown firmed to 3.8505 per mark, from its earlier 3.8525 and the 10-year yield gap with Germany narrowed to 94 basis points from 97 bp. --Kenneth Lund, Copenhagen newsroom, 45-33-969651
